0.0.n: A casual greeting used on its own here.

0.2.n: This is the speaker's name, written in hiragana.

0.3.n: A polite ending after a name; the speaker leaves out I.

1.0.n: This is the first character of the name きょん, not a form of 来る.

1.1.n: This fragment completes the name きょん and adds polite です; it is not a standalone word.

2.0.n: This fragment contains しん and the first character of きょん, the two names in the channel title.

2.1.n: These characters complete きょん, a name within the channel title; they are not a separate word.

2.2.n: An English loanword written in katakana, following the channel's name.

2.3.n: This polite ending completes the introduction of the channel.

3.0.n: Read きょう here; は makes it the topic of the sentence.

3.1.n: This is topic-marking は plus conversational ね, not the verb 跳ねる.

3.3.n: Here it refers to the urban streets where they will meet people.

3.4.n: Links 街中 to みなさん, identifying the people as those out in town.

3.5.n: A polite way to refer to the people they will approach.

3.6.n: Marks the following worries as belonging to みなさん.

3.7.n: The prefix お adds a respectful tone when referring to other people's concerns.

3.8.n: Shows that お悩み is what they will solve.

3.9.n: Adds a conversational pause and gently invites the listener's attention.

3.11.n: A general counting word, used here for individual problems.

3.12.n: After a quantity, this indicates repeating that amount for each step.

3.13.n: 解決する becomes 解決して, followed by いく to show the action progressing from now onward.

3.14.n: Introduces the stated plan as the content of the following ところ.

3.15.n: In というところで, this refers to their current plan or setup, not a physical place.

3.16.n: Ends the setup with a linking form, leaving the thought open for what follows.

4.0.n: The polite form of 解決する; the problems are understood and left unstated.

5.0.n: Read きょう here; it sets the time for their arrival.

5.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic; pronounced わ when used as this particle.

5.2.n: A place name for a district in Tokyo.

5.3.n: Marks Shibuya as the destination of their arrival.

5.4.n: A humble, polite past form of やってくる, using まいる in place of くる.

6.0.n: An English loanword used as a standalone exclamation; our is implied by context.

7.0.n: Repeats the previous speaker's word in a short, agreeing response.

8.0.n: A conversational opener that softens the statement.

8.1.n: A casual form of いろいろな that directly describes the following noun.

8.2.n: The respectful prefix お acknowledges other people's concerns; the subject marker が is omitted afterward.

8.3.n: 出る in its て-form plus くる describes problems emerging as they proceed.

8.4.n: Marks the preceding prediction as what the speaker thinks.

8.5.n: The polite form of 思う; the speaker does not explicitly say I.

8.6.n: Connects the expectation of varied problems to the confident promise that follows.

8.8.n: Refers to every problem; the object marker を is left out in this casual speech.

8.9.n: The polite form of 解決する expresses a confident commitment here.

9.0.n: A playful shout, treated as a stylized version of gotcha here rather than a standard Japanese word.

9.2.n: A playful rendering of English gotcha in katakana, echoing the preceding shout.

0.tip: Japanese introductions commonly omit I and simply put です after the speaker's name.

1.tip: Read きょん as one name; the supplied split does not reflect real word boundaries.

2.tip: The names しん and きょん combine into the channel title despite the misleading word splits.

3.lit: Today, you know, townspeople's worries, you know, one at a time, will go on solving—that being the setup.
3.tip: Verb て-form plus いく presents an action as progressing onward from now.

4.tip: Both we and the problems can be omitted because the previous line makes them clear.

5.lit: Today, as for, to Shibuya have come!
5.tip: やってまいりました is a humble, polite way to announce that you have arrived.

6.tip: A noun alone can work as an exclamation; Japanese does not need to explicitly include our here.

7.tip: Repeating a short expression can signal agreement without adding a full sentence.

8.lit: Well, various worries will come up, I think, but all will solve!
8.tip: A clause followed by と思います means I think that, with と marking the thought's content.

9.tip: These are playful shouts, not standard Japanese vocabulary you need to memorize.
